newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ICICI rules out takeover of Indian Bank.
newsitem.headline: India's ICICI rules out takeover of Indian Bank.

text.p: Indian term-lender Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India (ICICI) on Tuesday said it had no plans to take over Indian Bank, an unprofitable state-owned bank.
ICICI said in a statement that it was denying a newsagency report published in the Asian Wall Street Journal on Monday.
"ICICI has not received any proposal from the Government of India nor does it have any plans to take over Indian Bank," ICICI spokeswoman Kalpana Morparia said.

Indian Bank's chairman and a former general manager were arrested last year in investigations regarding their role in a 13.36-billion-rupee loss for the year ending March 31, 1996. Both have since been released on bail.

The agency report said that the takeover proposal, which originated with the Ministry of Finance and had been cleared by the office of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, would officially be announced within a few weeks' time.

Indian Bank, the country's seventh largest commercial bank, had total loans of 78.7 billion rupees and deposits of 133 billion rupees on March 31, 1996, and had an accumulated loss of 17.12 billion rupees.
